questions.question: What is the logit function and how does it relate to the Logit Normal distribution?
questions.expected_answer: The logit function is defined as log(x/(1-x)), which transforms probabilities from the range (0, 1) to the entire real line. In the context of the Logit Normal distribution, it is used to map a normally distributed random variable onto the range (0, 1).

full_credit: Correctly defines the logit function and its role in the Logit Normal distribution.
partial_credit: Mentions the logit function but lacks clarity on its application.
common_mistakes: Confusing the logit function with other transformations or distributions.

questions.question: Under the normal assumption H1, calculate P(0.9 < X < 1.0) given that X follows Normal(µ = 0.7, s² = 0.22).
questions.expected_answer: To find P(0.9 < X < 1.0), first standardize the values using Z = (X - µ) / s. Then use the standard normal table to find the probabilities corresponding to the Z-scores.
